  evidence 2: source ALB-S-0067, "11/10/98 Albright remarks to Naturalization Ceremony for New Citizens" (type primary; institution U.S. Department of State)
    url: https://1997-2001.state.gov/statements/1998/981110.html
    fetch_url: none
    registry: listed as U.S. Department of State; allowed types here: primary, institutional, secondary
    snapshot file: data/inductees/albright/snapshots/ALB-S-0067.txt (fetched by browser)

- quote_in_snapshot: true only if you opened each snapshot file and found each evidence quote in it, ignoring differences in case, whitespace, curly versus straight quotation marks, dashes and soft hyphens. false if any quote is missing or any file cannot be read.
- live_by_source: one entry for each source of the item (each evidence source; for a reconstruction each basis source), with source_id, the url you checked, and result "found" if you loaded that live source and every passage quoted from it is there, "not_found" if it loaded and a passage is missing, "unreachable" if you could not load or read it. Do not answer "found" from the snapshot file.
- entailed: true only if the quotes, taken together, state everything in the claim, including the date and place shown with it.
- adds_information: true if the claim, its date or its place adds anything the quotes do not state: a date, number, name, place, order of events, cause, motive, superlative or evaluative word. "refuted" if a quote or statement is missing (in a snapshot or a live source), or the evidence contradicts or does not support the record. Otherwise "unclear".
rationale: at most two sentences naming the specific problem, or "no problem found".
registry_suggestion: null, unless a source not listed in the authority registry is published by an archive, museum, government body, university, foundation or prize body that could be listed; then one line naming the publisher, its domain and the type it could have (for example "fi.edu: The Franklin Institute, institutional"). It is advice for a person who maintains the registry: it never changes another field or the verdict.

It applies only to a source whose registry standing is the Library of Congress (loc.gov) or the U.S. National Archives (archives.gov), and only to the holder's own rights field in that source's snapshot. LoC's full wording "No known restrictions on images made by the U.S. Government; images copied from other sources may be restricted" (its second clause is part of the phrase, not a caveat) means public-domain only when the same LoC record gives positive evidence of government creation (its part_of or a creator with the role creator is Historic American Buildings Survey, Historic American Landscapes Survey, Historic American Engineering Record, or a "United States. <agency>" heading), no item field marks an outside entry ("challenge", "competition", "contest", "prize", as in a "HALS Challenge Entry"), every named creator or contributor carries a government affiliation in its own heading (a federal survey or a "United States. <agency>" heading; a staff role such as photographer alone is not enough; an owner, architect or other role blocks it). Owner decision 2026-10-18: in a record made by a federal survey (HABS, HAER, HALS), a name with no role is an associated person (such as a family member), not a maker, and when the record lists the survey's team (project manager, field team, field team supervisor) its photographer and historian count as survey staff. For an item that is one image file of the record, the titles of the record's other image files are not read for copy markers (the item's own file title and title are), and nothing in the record's title, notes, description, credits or image titles and captions says the image is a copy ("photocopy", "photocopies", "photocopied", "copied from", "copy of", "copy photograph", "recopy", "recopied", "photograph of a photograph", "reproduction of"); otherwise never usable. Leffler, Thomas J. O'Halloran, Marion S. Trikosko, John Bledsoe, Chick Harrity; otherwise the item is never usable. "No known copyright restriction" means public-domain only when the same LoC record is in the New York World-Telegram & Sun collection and credits a World-Telegram staff photographer (a photographer named in its creator or contributor field, "photo by <name>", or record text such as "staff photograph", "World-Telegram photo", "World-Telegram & Sun photo"); otherwise never usable. A record that credits a wire service or agency (Associated Press, AP Photo, AP Wirephoto, Wirephoto, Acme, United Press, UPI, International News Photo, INP, Underwood, Harris & Ewing, Wide World, Keystone, Bain News, Pacific & Atlantic) is never a staff photograph. An approved wording followed by a caveat that asserts a restriction ("may be restricted", "restrictions apply", "restrictions may apply", "copyright restrictions", "permission required", "permission is required", "not in the public domain", "may be protected", "privacy and publicity rights") is never usable; a following sentence that supports free status (such as "No renewal in Copyright office (checked ...)") or only points to more information ("For more information, see ...") does not block it. Otherwise it is link-only: license_class must be unknown or rights-restricted. A National Archives "Unrestricted" use or access status alone is not a rights grant for such an item; it grants public-domain only to records created by the federal government. The media record carries authorship: kind private or federal, each author with a death year and the verified fact or authority-record quote that backs it, and optionally the publication year with its basis.
